consular.notes: Australia doesn't have an embassy in the Dominican Republic. The Embassy of Canada in Santo Domingo provides consular assistance for Australians. It can issue Australian provisional travel documents. - Special travel documents (Australian Passport Office) You can also get consular assistance from the Australian Embassy in Mexico City.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. This includes long prison sentences in local jails. Authorities may arrest you for illegal drugs if you're either: carrying even a very small amount of drugs, or with someone who's using them If you're found driving under the influence of alcohol or other drugs, authorities will arrest and possibly detain you. Border officials may screen you for drugs, including on departure. - Carrying and using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Avoid public displays of affection. Same-sex relationships are legal in Dominican Republic , but the country is conservative. Same-sex marriages aren't recognised in Dominican Republic. It's not illegal to discriminate based on sexual orientation or gender identity.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: No visa in advance for a tourist visit: buy a tourist card on arrival, valid for 30 days, and complete the electronic entry and exit form (e-Ticket).
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Tourist card bought on arrival (30 days) plus the online e-Ticket entry and exit form.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Complete the e-Ticket entry and exit form online. If travelling through the US or Canada, meet their entry or transit rules. The land borders with Haiti are closed.
visa-preparation.useful_stay: 30 days on the tourist card; for longer visits an extra fee is paid at the airport on departure.

steps.step: Complete the electronic entry and exit form (e-Ticket) before arriving and before leaving.
Buy the tourist card on arrival; it's valid for 30 days.
Staying longer than 30 days: pay the extra fee at the airport when departing.
Check whether the departure tax is included in the airline ticket.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Ask locally. Dominican Republic Ministry of Tourism: beachwear is for the beach, pool and resort only. Cover up in streets, shops and restaurants, especially in Santo Domingo. For churches such as the Basílica de Higüey, cover shoulders and knees; no shorts, tank tops or beachwear.
